ai.description: This snake reaches 30–40 cm. It is uniform dark brown to black with a glossy sheen and a pale, yellow-spotted belly. It features a blunt, shovel-shaped tail and small, smooth, iridescent scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Karnataka Burrowing Snake is best distinguished by its lack of a preocular scale, meaning the prefrontal scales make direct contact with the eye.
ai.habitat: The Karnataka burrowing snake inhabits the moist, leaf-littered floors of evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Karnataka burrowing snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time hidden beneath leaf litter or soil to avoid surface predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Pseudoplectrurus canaricus* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season in the Western Ghats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Pseudoplectrurus canaricus* is endemic to the high-elevation evergreen forests of the central Western Ghats in the Indian state of Karnataka.
